A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPU–FPGA memory-processing research. All 23 pages of each version, including the figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison despite the title change and layout revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original latency profiling, GPU–FPGA performance comparisons, energy measurements, and batch-size analyses in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the latency comparisons and energy and batch-size results in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The four-stage pipeline, GPU–FPGA allocation, fused kernels, memory hierarchy, and GPU fallback procedures remain unchanged. The added explanations and redrawn architecture diagrams do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: The same sparse-attention, RAG, MemAgent, Memory-as-Context, and TTT/LaCT workloads and source datasets remain. The new V80 discussion concerns hardware scaling rather than additional data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including the GPU-centric implementations, BM25S retrieval baseline, and A100 comparisons. The V80 estimate concerns a configuration of the proposed system, not a new competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix H.1 adds a synthesis-informed evaluation of migration from U55C to V80, introducing an additional hardware configuration assessed through extrapolation. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; no physical V80 system measurement is reported.

E4.justification: Appendix H.1 adds a limited device-scaling analysis addressing the benefits of newer FPGA hardware. Figure 13 also revises part of the arithmetic-intensity analysis. Existing batch-scaling, communication-overhead, and kernel analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point estimates and geometric-mean summaries. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the V80 projection does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 13 lowers the plotted 'Remaining Ops in LLM' arithmetic intensity for DeepSeek Attention and LServe/SeerAttention-R from several hundred to approximately 20 FLOPs/byte. Appendix H.1 adds an estimated additional 1.6× geometric-mean end-to-end speedup from V80 migration. Existing latency, energy, and batch-size results otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 and the mathematical mappings for the four pipeline stages are unchanged. The added framework and hardware-scaling discussions introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The three central claims—unified memory processing, computational heterogeneity, and heterogeneous acceleration—remain intact. The abstract summarizes performance using the retained maxima rather than full ranges, without changing the underlying contribution or headline performance limits.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds explanations of the abstraction's analytical purpose, stage bypassing, and kernel reuse. Appendix H.1 expands the newer-hardware applicability argument through scratchpad and irregular-access considerations while acknowledging the absence of current-generation system profiling. The added PCIe discussion largely repeats existing Appendix C.1 material.

D1.justification: v2 adds a HeteroLLM repository pointer in the page-2 footnote and additional hardware context, including V80's stated 94 MB scratchpad capacity, in Appendix H.1. Existing implementation instructions and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning in the background and Appendix A remain unchanged. The reference list matches after accounting for pagination and formatting.

P1.justification: The title replaces 'Disaggregated LLM' with 'Large Language Model'; the abstract and selected passages are edited, and short explanatory passages and Appendix H.1 are added. v2 also adds financial-interest and funding disclosures and updates publication text. Most prose and the main organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2, 6, and 7 are redrawn with revised typography and spacing. Several existing displays are resized or relocated, including Figure 9, Table 3, and the final appendix plots. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency and usability through the repository pointer, financial-interest and funding disclosures, clearer diagrams, and additional framework explanations. The main empirical evidence is preserved. The gains remain limited: the V80 speedup is a synthesis-based projection without integrated-system validation, and the Figure 13 numerical revisions are not explained.
